title: Redwood POC scoping w/ Cedarcrest Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a limited pilot. Discussed SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logging, KMS/HSM, VPC/private deployment options, and success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy). Agreed next steps: Redwood to send security pack and SOC/ISO attestations, schedule technical deep dive and benchmark window, customer to provide sample workload and HIPAA boundary doc.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
next_steps: Jordan Keller - send SOC 2 and ISO attestation + security pack (network diagrams, audit log samples) - due 2026-12-24

Mark Evans - share HIPAA boundary doc and list of required audit fields for pilot - due 2026-12-27

action_items: Jordan Keller: email SOC2/ISO + security pack (24th Dec)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Redwood SE), Mark (CISO), Susan (Head of AI), Liam (IT Ops), Tanya (Privacy Counsel)

[00:00] Jordan Keller: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i'm Jordan from Redwood inference, alex and priya are with me from engineering. um Mark, Susan, thanks for carving out time.
[00:18] Mark Evans: yeah thanks. the team's mainly curious about the security posture for a pilot — we want to run a limited POC that processes de-identified clinical notes but there are e phi considerations so we need to validate controls.
[00:36] Priya Nair: great, and to be explicit we'll go through SOC 2 / ISO evidence, SSO integration, RBAC, audit logs, and also sizing and benchmarks so you can see perf/cost tradeoffs.
[00:52] Susan Park: ideal pilot for us is 2-4 weeks, validate latency at p50/p90/p99 for our common prompts and confirm that model outputs meet our accuracy thresholds. also we want to prove we can keep data in our VPC or use a dedicated instance — compliance is non-negotiable.
[01:12] Alex Chen: quick clarifying q — when you say "keep data in our VPC" do you mean full private deployment or VPC peering to a private control plane?
[01:26] Liam Rivera: we'd prefer a private deployment if possible, but we can start with Redwood Dedicated if you have strong egress controls and KMS integration. primary ask is no customer PII persisted beyond retention windows and strong audit logs.
[01:42] Jordan Keller: understood. for pilots we commonly do one of three: hosted (fastest), dedicated (reserved capacity in our infra with stronger isolation), or private (VPC or on-prem). For Cedarcrest Health given HIPAA concerns, we recommend dedicated or private.
[02:00] Mark Evans: show me the SOC 2 stuff — do you have an attestation and scope? we need to know which controls map to our audit requirements.
[02:12] Priya Nair: yes — we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestations. i'll attach the reports but note there are redactions for vendor details. the pack also includes our control matrix mapping to common healthcare requirements.
[02:28] Tanya Morales: are those publicly available or do we need an NDA?
[02:34] Jordan Keller: we can share the SOC 2 and ISO summary under NDA or via our secure document portal; for initial review we can provide the summary and a control mapping. full reports usually under MSA/NDA.
[02:48] Susan Park: for encryption — we need details on KMS and HSM usage, key rotation, and whether customer-managed keys are supported.
[02:58] Priya Nair: customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. keys can be in your cloud KMS or an HSM, and we support bring-your-own key material for most cloud providers. for hosted, we offer managed keys but can discuss a BYOK arrangement for pilot under certain contracts.
[03:15] Mark Evans: logging: we need immutable audit logs with user IDs, request metadata, response hashes, and retention for 7 years. does Redwood's audit log include request/response payloads or just metadata?
[03:30] Alex Chen: out of the box we record request metadata (timestamp, user, model, tokens, latency) and structured audit events. payload logging (full response) is configurable and can be disabled; for ePHI you'd typically avoid storing full payloads and instead log hashes and metadata. we also support streaming logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or cloud logging endpoints.
[03:52] Liam Rivera: ok good. how granular is RBAC — we need role separation between dev, ops, and analysts, plus support for SCIM provisioning from Okta.
[04:05] Priya Nair: RBAC is role-based with customizable roles and permissions; SCIM and SAML SSO with Okta/Azure AD supported. we can provision groups and map to roles; for the pilot we usually create a small set of roles: admin, engineer, auditor, and readonly analyst.
[04:22] Jordan Keller: timeline question — Susan suggested 2-4 weeks. operationally, a 3-week pilot where week 1 is baseline config and onboarding, week 2 is benchmark runs and integration, week 3 is analysis and decisioning — does that map to your expectations?
[04:38] Susan Park: yes that sounds reasonable. success criteria: p99 latency under 800ms for our core prompt (avg tokens ~400), throughput of ~25 concurrent requests with acceptable tail latency, accuracy measured by our eval suite (we'll provide test prompts and pass/fail thresholds).
[04:58] Priya Nair: that's clear. can you share approximate qps, average and max tokens, and concurrency? we'll size the Dedicated pool or private instance accordingly.
[05:10] Mark Evans: during peak hours internal tool makes about 20 qps, avg payload 350 tokens, but peaks can spike to 60 qps for short windows. we want the pilot to model typical plus 2x burst.
[05:24] Priya Nair: noted — for those numbers we'd recommend starting the pilot on 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (or CPU-optimized quantized stack) depending on model choice; we'll propose exact instance sizing in the benchmark plan.
[05:40] Liam Rivera: question on model artifacts and where they live — do you allow us to pin a model version and have it pulled into our private VPC?
[05:50] Alex Chen: yes, model version pinning is supported; for private deployments we stage model artifacts in a private registry within the customer's network or an encrypted object store with scoped access. deployment automation can run via your infra.
[06:04] Mark Evans: auditability and chain of custody for model updates is important — we need logs that show model version, who triggered deploys, and diffs between versions.
[06:14] Priya Nair: we have model deployment audit events and rollout traces; can export deployment histories and tie back to users. we can include this in the pilot checklist.
[06:24] Susan Park: benchmarks — what's the typical benchmark methodology? we want reproducible runs and a scriptable harness.
[06:32] Priya Nair: we'll provide a benchmark harness (python scripts + k6 wrapper) that runs synthetic and real prompts, captures latency distributions, token counts, and cost metrics. we'll also run multiple repeats and report p50/p90/p99 and average token cost. you'll be able to run it from your network against the pilot endpoints.
[06:52] Jordan Keller: there may be occasional transcription typos in these notes but i'll summarize precisely in email.
[06:58] [08:03] Mark Evans: how about data residency and storage — logs stored in your region or can they stream to our cloud?
[08:12] Alex Chen: logs can stream to your cloud logging endpoint (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Log Analytics) and we can scope retention there. for private deployments, all storage remains in your cloud account.
[08:24] Tanya Morales: any emerging concerns: does Redwood offer HIPAA BAAs or specific agreement for PHI?
[08:33] Jordan Keller: yes Redwood supports HIPAA agreements for enterprise customers; for a pilot we'll do a limited BAA appendix and scope it to the pilot environment. full production BAA is standard for Dedicated/Private Enterprise contracts.
[08:47] Priya Nair: one operational note: please avoid sending raw PHI during initial benchmark — use de-identified or hashed payloads. we can do a small controlled run with tokenized sample.
[08:58] Susan Park: understood. for the pilot success criteria I'll restate: 1) p99 latency <800ms for our core flows, 2) throughput supports 25 concurrent steady-state and tolerates 2x burst, 3) audit logs include required fields, 4) SSO + SCIM provisioning work for our Okta instance, and 5) we can enforce RBAC and key control via our KMS.
[09:22] Priya Nair: good checklist — we'll bake that into the pilot success criteria doc.
[09:29] Mark Evans: pricing/pilot cost — what is typical for this sort of test?
[09:35] Jordan Keller: we usually do a time-boxed pilot with a small committed spend to cover dedicated capacity and engineering support; i'll send a proposed SOW with costs for 3-week pilot (compute + support hours + optional dedicated infra).
[09:49] Alex Chen: regarding failover — if performance degradation occurs we can auto-fallback to a smaller model or route to a hosted endpoint; this will be part of the runbook we propose.
[09:58] Liam Rivera: any pre-reqs from our side for Okta SAML/SCIM setup?
[10:04] Priya Nair: just an Okta admin and a test account; we'll give SAML metadata and SCIM token instructions. provisioning usually takes <1 day once we have admin access.
[10:15] Susan Park: next, can you outline the benchmark schedule?
[10:18] Priya Nair: proposed: Day 0-2 onboarding and access + config; Day 3 run baseline synthetic tests; Day 4-7 run real workload tests (off-hours to limit production impact); Day 8-10 soak/run bursts; Day 11 analysis and report. we can compress if needed.
[10:39] Mark Evans: will you need any firewall exceptions or IP allow-lists?
[10:44] Alex Chen: yes we'll give a list of Redwood egress IPs for dedicated/pilot endpoints or a VPN tunnel for private deployments. for hosted pilot we give TLS endpoints and you can restrict by API keys.
[10:56] Jordan Keller: okay let's capture the concrete action items — i'll send the SOC/ISO summaries and the SOW plus the benchmark harness. Priya will send the benchmark plan and expected sizing. Mark/Tanya will provide HIPAA boundary and required audit fields.
[11:10] Tanya Morales: we'll review the SOC summary and get back with any gaps; also want to confirm retention and deletion procedures in writing.
[11:18] Jordan Keller: yes we'll include retention/delete SLA in the pilot appendix.
[11:22] Susan Park: when can we run the actual benchmark? earliest after holiday window? we prefer second week of jan.
[11:30] Jordan Keller: we can aim week of Jan 11; i'll propose calendar invites after sending SOW.
[11:35] Mark Evans: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[11:38] Jordan Keller: quick recap then close — i'll email: SOC 2/ISO summaries, SOW for 3-week pilot, benchmark harness and runner, and a request for sample/de-identified dataset plus Okta admin contact. we'll schedule the technical deep dive for early Jan.
[11:53] Alex Chen: action owners noted in chat. thanks all.

[End of transcript]
